title: AI Enrollment Agent RFP: 40 Questions to Ask Vendors
summary: A copyable RFP for AI enrollment agents: 40 vendor questions, what good answers look like, a scoring rubric and a 60-day pilot plan for universities.
body_markdown:
A good RFP for an AI enrollment agent asks each vendor to prove five things: how fast it replies, whether it remembers students across text, voice, email and chat, how it hands students to human advisors, what it writes back to your CRM, and how it stays compliant. Below are 40 questions you can copy into a procurement document, what a good answer looks like for each section, a scoring rubric, and a 30 to 60 day pilot plan.


The questions are vendor-neutral, so you can send them to anyone, including us. Our own answers are at the end, labeled. A structured RFP matters because the demos all look the same. In UPCEA's December 2025 secret shopper study, **44% of 1,000 inquiries got no response** . Every vendor will say it fixes that. These questions make them show how.


If you're still deciding which category of tool you need, start with[admissions chatbot vs AI enrollment agent](https://www.apten.ai/blog/admissions-chatbot-vs-ai-enrollment-agent) . That post has the vendor list and a short set of demo questions. This one is the procurement version.


## How should you structure an AI enrollment agent RFP?


Group questions by what can break in production, not by vendor feature lists. Ten sections cover it. For each one, ask for evidence in one of three forms: a live test you run yourself, a document (a report, contract or sample record), or data from the vendor's existing customers.


Two rules make answers comparable. Require a yes, no or partial before any narrative, so "on our roadmap" can't hide inside a paragraph. And ask vendors to flag answers that depend on configuration your team builds. Three weeks of your CRM admin's time is a cost.


## Channels and cross-channel memory


1.


Which channels does the agent use to talk to students today: SMS, voice (inbound and outbound), email, webchat? Which are live and which are beta?


2.


If a student texts a question and calls two days later, does the agent on the call know what was said by text? Show this live.


3.


Can the agent move a text conversation to a live phone call mid-thread, either right away or at a time the student picks?


4.


When a call goes unanswered, what does the agent do next on other channels, and how does it detect voicemail?


**What a good answer looks like.** One conversation record per student that every channel reads from and writes to. The vendor runs the text-then-call test in front of you without a script. Watch for products that send on several channels from separate tools, where each channel keeps its own history. That's multichannel sending, not multichannel memory.[Our guide to AI voice agents for student enrollment](https://www.apten.ai/blog/best-ai-voice-agents-student-enrollment) goes deeper on the voice side.


## Speed and availability


1.


What is your median time from RFI submission to first reply, and what share of inquiries get a reply within one minute? Give the cohort, date range and how you measured it.


2.


Does the agent reply at the same speed at 11 p.m. on a Saturday and during a start-date surge?


3.


How fast does the agent answer an inbound text or call from a student who already exists in the system?


4.


What is your uptime over the last 12 months, and what happens to queued messages during an outage?


**What a good answer looks like.** Numbers from production, with the method shown. For example, Apten's platform data shows a 7-second median first reply and 98% of new inquiries answered within a minute, from July 28 to October 25, 2026. Expect that specificity from every vendor: how many schools, which dates, and what counts as a reply. Then submit test RFIs on a weekend night and time them. For the benchmarks behind response speed, see[speed-to-lead benchmarks for 2026](https://www.apten.ai/blog/speed-to-lead-benchmarks-2026) .


## Handoff to human advisors


1.


Can the agent warm-transfer a student to an admissions advisor from a text thread, a webchat and a live AI call?


2.


What does the advisor see before or during the transfer? Share a sample summary.


3.


What happens when no advisor answers: fallback number, a text to the student, a scheduled callback?


4.


Which triggers send a conversation to a human (student asks, low confidence, upset student, specific topics), and can we change them?


**What a good answer looks like.** Transfers from every channel the agent works, a summary the advisor gets before saying hello, and a defined path when the advisor misses the call. A vendor that can't tell you its transfer connect rate isn't measuring it. The full mechanics are in[how a warm transfer from AI to an admissions advisor should work](https://www.apten.ai/blog/ai-handoff-to-admissions-advisor-warm-transfer) .


## CRM integration and write-back


1.


Which CRMs do you integrate with natively (Slate, Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, HubSpot, Element451, others)? Which need custom work or middleware?


2.


Exactly which fields and objects does the agent write back: transcripts, summaries, status, tags, opt-outs, appointments, tasks? Show a real record after a test conversation.


3.


How does the agent pick up new RFIs (real-time push, polling, file import), and what's the delay?


4.


Can a CRM field change, like an application started or a missing document, trigger a follow-up from the agent?


**What a good answer looks like.** A named list of CRMs, the fields written to each, and a sample record from a sandbox. "We integrate with everything" usually means a webhook and your developer's time. Watch the direction too. A tool that writes back only a transcript blob leaves advisors reading paragraphs instead of filtering on a status field.


## Guardrails, accuracy and misrepresentation risk


1.


Where do the agent's answers come from, and can we restrict it to approved content for tuition, financial aid, transfer credit, accreditation and job outcomes?


2.


Are our guardrails checked before a message sends, or reviewed afterward?


3.


What does the agent do when it doesn't know an answer?


4.


Can we review flagged conversations and see which rule blocked a message?


**What a good answer looks like.** Pre-send checks you configure, a clear "I don't know, let me connect you" behavior, and an audit trail. This matters more in higher ed than in most industries. Under 34 CFR 668.71, the Department of Education can hold an institution responsible for misrepresentations made by any party it contracts with for marketing, recruiting or admissions services. An AI agent you hire to recruit falls inside that. Test it in the demo by asking about job placement rates and whether credits will transfer.


## Compliance: TCPA, opt-outs, quiet hours, 10DLC, FERPA and AI disclosure


1.


Which parts of TCPA compliance does your product handle, and which stay with us? State plainly who captures consent and who scrubs against Do Not Call lists.


2.


How does the agent detect opt-outs (STOP keywords and natural-language requests like "please stop texting me"), and does an opt-out on one channel stop the others? How fast does it sync to our CRM?


3.


Are quiet hours configurable, and are they applied in the student's time zone or ours?


4.


Who registers our A2P 10DLC brand and campaign, and what's the typical timeline to approval?


5.


What will you sign to support our FERPA obligations (data processing terms, use limits, no training on our student data), and how do you handle the school-official conditions?


6.


Does the agent disclose that it's an AI, at the start or when asked, and can we set that behavior by state?


**What a good answer looks like.** A vendor that tells you what it doesn't do. Consent capture and DNC scrubbing usually sit with the institution, and a vendor who implies otherwise is a risk. Opt-outs need to work fast. Since April 11, 2025, the FCC requires callers and texters to honor revocations made by any reasonable means within 10 business days. A broader "revoke-all" rule is delayed until January 31, 2027. Calls with AI-generated voices count as artificial voice calls under the TCPA, per the FCC's February 2024 ruling, so they need prior express consent. On disclosure, Utah requires businesses to tell people they're talking to generative AI when asked, and California's bot law bars bots from hiding what they are to drive a sale. More detail is in our[2026 TCPA and state AI law guide](https://www.apten.ai/blog/ai-compliance-guide-2026-tcpa-fcc-state-laws) , our[A2P 10DLC guide](https://www.apten.ai/blog/a2p-dlc-compliance-2026) , and our post on[FERPA and AI agents that talk to prospective students](https://www.apten.ai/blog/ferpa-ai-agents-prospective-students) .


For FERPA specifically, the Department of Education lets a vendor act as a "school official" only if it performs a service your staff would otherwise do, stays under your direct control over use and maintenance of records, uses the data only for the purpose it was shared, and meets the criteria in your annual notification. Your contract is what makes those conditions true.


## Security


1.


Do you have a current SOC 2 Type II report, and will you share it under NDA? What period does it cover?


2.


Is data encrypted at rest and in transit?


3.


What is your default retention period for conversations and recordings, and can we delete a student's data on request? Describe how.


4.


List your subprocessors, including LLM, speech and telephony providers, and say whether any of them can train on our data.


**What a good answer looks like.** A SOC 2 Type II report, not a Type I or a "we're in progress." Type II tests whether controls actually worked over a period of months. Retention answers should name the default, the deletion path and how long backups keep data. The subprocessor list matters because an AI agent sends conversation data to more third parties than a CRM does.


## Reporting


1.


Which metrics do you report out of the box: first reply time, contact rate, appointments set, transfers attempted and connected, opt-outs?


2.


Can we break those down by program of interest, lead source and start term?


3.


Can we export raw conversation and event data, or only dashboards?


4.


Can you report outcomes downstream of the agent (app started, app submitted, enrolled) by joining with our CRM data?


**What a good answer looks like.** Definitions for every metric, the same breakdowns your enrollment team already uses, and a raw export. If a vendor can't show you the definition of "contacted," you can't compare its numbers with anyone else's.


## Pilot design


1.


Will you run a 30 to 60 day pilot against a holdout group, and who pays for it?


2.


What setup do you need from us, and how many weeks before live traffic?


3.


Will you agree to written success criteria before the pilot starts, with an exit if they're missed?


**What a good answer looks like.** Yes to a holdout, a setup estimate in weeks with named tasks on your side, and success criteria in writing. The pilot plan further down gives you the metrics to use.


## Pricing model


1.


What's the pricing model: annual license, per seat, per minute, per contact or per conversation?


2.


What's the all-in first-year cost, including carrier SMS fees, phone numbers, 10DLC registration, integration and implementation hours?


3.


What happens to cost if our inquiry volume doubles in a start-date surge, or drops by half?


**What a good answer looks like.** One number for year one with every line item, and a price that moves predictably with volume. Per-contact pricing tracks inquiry volume. Per-minute pricing can spike when the agent places more calls. Neither is wrong, but you should be able to model both against last year's RFI counts.


## How do you score AI enrollment vendors?


Score each section 0 to 3 and multiply by a weight. Adjust the weights to your situation. A school with a large phone-based call center might weight handoff higher. A school under a compliance review might weight guardrails higher.


Section Weight 0: Missing 1: Weak 2: Solid 3: Strong


Channels and memory 15% One channel Several channels, separate histories Shared record, partial on one channel Shared record on every channel, shown live


Speed and availability 10% No data Claims without method Production data, one cohort Production data with method, confirmed by your test RFIs


Handoff to humans 15% Form or ticket only Cold transfer from voice Warm transfer with summary Warm transfer from every channel, defined fallback, connect rate reported


CRM write-back 15% Manual export Transcript only Mapped fields on your CRM Mapped fields plus CRM-triggered follow-ups, shown in your sandbox


Guardrails and accuracy 15% None Prompt instructions only Pre-send checks Pre-send checks, approved-content limits, audit trail


Compliance 10% Unclear ownership Keyword opt-outs only Cross-channel opt-outs, quiet hours All of that, plus student-time-zone quiet hours, 10DLC help and clear ownership


Security 10% No report SOC 2 Type I or in progress SOC 2 Type II Type II plus clear retention, deletion and subprocessor list


Reporting 5% None Dashboard only Defined metrics, breakdowns Defined metrics plus raw export


Pricing clarity 5% No quote Partial quote All-in year one All-in year one with volume scenarios


A vendor with 2s everywhere beats one with a few 3s and a 0. You'll spend next year working around the 0.


## What should you measure in a 30 to 60 day pilot?


Split new RFIs at random between the agent and your current process. Assigning by odd and even lead ID is good enough. Keep everything else the same: lead sources, advisors, start terms. Track five numbers for both.


Metric Definition to agree on Why it matters


Speed to first reply Median minutes from RFI submission to first non-automated reply, including nights and weekends The UPCEA data shows this is where most programs lose students first


Contact rate Share of RFIs where the student replied on any channel within 7 days Shows whether the agent starts real conversations, not just sends messages


Appointments set Share of RFIs with an advisor appointment or info session booked The step closest to an application that the agent controls directly


Transfer acceptance Share of warm transfers where an advisor connected with the student A transfer nobody answers costs you the student's trust


Opt-out rate Share of contacted students who opted out on any channel Catches aggressive cadences before they hurt deliverability or your reputation


Set targets before day one. If the agent group's first reply is measured in seconds while the holdout is measured in hours, the setup is working. If not, something is wrong. Track app starts and submissions for both groups too, but expect them to lag, because a 60-day pilot often ends before those students reach a start date. If your own scheduling system records attendance, compare show rates between the groups from that data.


Run the pilot through at least one inquiry spike if you can, such as a campaign launch or the weeks before a start date. Our post on[why college inquiries go unanswered](https://www.apten.ai/blog/college-inquiries-go-unanswered-speed-to-lead) covers what happens to response times when volume jumps.


## How would Apten answer some of these?


Since we're asking you to send this list to every vendor, here's how we'd answer a few of the questions ourselves.


-


**Channels and memory (1 to 4).** One agent works SMS, voice, email and webchat with a single conversation record. It can start a call from a text thread right away or schedule one. Missed calls get an automatic text follow-up, and the agent detects voicemail.


-


**Handoff (9 to 11).** Warm transfer works from SMS, webchat and live voice, with a summary for the advisor. If nobody picks up, it tries your fallback number if you've set one, then texts the student the transfer number and can schedule a callback.


-


**CRM (13, 14).** Native integrations with Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, HubSpot and Close. Write-back uses mapped fields, such as tags, an AI summary, qualified, replied, transferred and opt-outs. On Salesforce and Dynamics, field changes such as a missing application item can trigger follow-ups through automations your team sets up.


-


**Compliance (21 to 24).** Opt-outs are caught by STOP keywords and by AI detection of plain-language requests, and they're tracked per channel. Quiet hours are configurable and apply in the student's time zone. We help you get A2P 10DLC registration approved as a service. Consent capture and DNC scrubbing stay with your team.


-


**Security (27, 28).** Apten has a SOC 2 Type II report and encrypts data at rest and in transit.


-


**Booking.** The agent books on Google Calendar or shares your Calendly link, and sends a reminder before the appointment.


Send us the full list and we'll answer all 40.


## The bottom line


Copy the 40 questions, cut the ones that don't fit, and send the same document to every vendor on your shortlist. Score the answers with the rubric, pick the top two, and make them earn the contract in a pilot against a holdout group. A demo shows you what a vendor wants you to see. Sixty days of your own RFIs shows you what you'd actually get.
